sections.content: Conditional structures connect a possible situation with its consequence. For realistic future conditions, Spanish commonly uses si + present with a future or imperative result. For hypothetical situations, the imperfect subjunctive combines with the conditional. Travel problems naturally invite both patterns: a realistic plan for a possible delay and a hypothetical alternative if the original plan fails.

items.spanish: Si perdemos el tren, cogeremos el siguiente.
items.english: If we miss the train, we will take the next one.

items.spanish: Si hay una alternativa, cambiaremos de ruta.
items.english: If there is an alternative, we will change route.

items.spanish: Si perdiéramos la conexión, tendríamos que buscar otro alojamiento.
items.english: If we missed the connection, we would have to find other accommodation.

items.spanish: Si tuviera más tiempo, viajaría por la costa.
items.english: If I had more time, I would travel along the coast.

sections.content: Do not use the conditional directly after si for these standard conditional patterns. The realistic pattern is si + present; the hypothetical pattern is si + imperfect subjunctive + conditional.
